I-Mab is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing antibody-based cancer immunotherapies, with a lead bispecific candidate called givastomig aimed at gastric and other solid tumours. It began in China, later moved its headquarters to Rockville, Maryland, and is listed on Nasdaq (IMAB). It earns no meaningful product sales yet and is funded by equity raises and partnerships; Crunchbase shows about $880 million raised in total. Ultimate customers would be hospitals and patients, but today it deals with pharma partners and investors. B2B biotech with little consumer brand awareness.

Immunome is a clinical-stage biotechnology company based in Bothell, Washington, developing targeted cancer therapies, notably antibody-drug conjugates and radioligand-style oncology programs, after building its early platform on antibodies derived from the immune systems of cancer survivors. It is listed on Nasdaq (IMNM) and has no large commercial revenue; it funds itself through equity offerings, with Crunchbase showing roughly $1 billion raised in total. Future customers are oncologists, hospitals and health systems. A biotech with no consumer brand awareness and limited relevance outside investor and healthcare circles.

insightsoftware is a provider of financial reporting, planning, analytics and performance-management software for finance teams, selling products such as Hubble, Jet Reports, Logi Analytics and Izenda, largely built through acquisitions. Customers are mid-market and large enterprises that pay subscriptions and licences, mostly in the Office of the CFO. It is headquartered in Raleigh, North Carolina, with offices worldwide and thousands of customers. Privately held and backed by private equity (Genstar, TA Associates, Hg). A B2B software brand with little consumer awareness, though it has the budget of a large software vendor.

Isotopen Technologien Muenchen (ITM) is a radiopharmaceutical company based in Garching near Munich, Germany, developing and supplying targeted radionuclide therapies for cancer, including its lead candidate ITM-11 (lutetium-177 edotreotide) for neuroendocrine tumours, and supplying medical isotopes such as lutetium-177. Customers are hospitals, nuclear medicine departments and pharma partners. It is privately held and has raised large private rounds, roughly $1 billion in total per Crunchbase, including a 2025 financing. B2B pharma and isotope supplier with no consumer brand awareness.

Kailera Therapeutics is a US biotech based in Waltham, Massachusetts, developing next-generation injectable and oral treatments for obesity and related metabolic conditions, working with GLP-1 type drug candidates licensed from Chinese developer Hengrui. It launched in 2024 and raised a large Series B of about $600 million, with roughly $1 billion in total funding. It has no marketed product yet; revenue would come from drug sales to patients through healthcare systems. Private, venture-backed. No consumer brand yet, but it targets the very large obesity-drug market.

Kirkland & Ellis is one of the world's largest and highest-grossing law firms, headquartered in Chicago with offices across the US, Europe and Asia. It advises on private equity, M&A, restructuring, litigation and intellectual property, and is especially dominant with private equity sponsors. Clients are corporations, funds and financial institutions paying hourly and project fees; revenue is in the region of several billion dollars, with thousands of lawyers. Privately held partnership, founded in 1909. Strong reputation among executives and dealmakers but no consumer brand profile; a B2B professional-services firm with deep pockets.

Kriya Therapeutics is a biotechnology company based in the Research Triangle area of North Carolina (Morrisville), developing gene therapies for common diseases such as diabetes, obesity, eye disease and other chronic conditions, using adeno-associated virus vectors to deliver durable treatment. It is private and venture-backed, with about $920 million raised in total per Crunchbase, including a large 2025 round. It has no marketed product yet and earns no meaningful revenue. Future customers are patients via hospitals and health systems. A B2B biotech with no consumer brand awareness.

Madinet Masr is an Egyptian real estate developer based in Cairo, best known for the large Taj Misr and Sarai master-planned communities in New Cairo, with residential, commercial and mixed-use projects. Customers are Egyptian home buyers and investors, and it makes money from selling units and land. It is a long-established developer (founded in 1959) and is listed on the Egyptian Exchange. Crunchbase shows about $1 billion in funding or financing. Regional property brand known in Egypt, with limited visibility abroad; possible interest from a Middle East and Africa market angle.

Omeros is a Seattle-based biopharmaceutical company focused on drugs for complement-mediated and other immune disorders, with its lead candidate narsoplimab (a MASP-2 inhibitor) for transplant-associated thrombotic microangiopathy. It previously sold the eye-surgery drug Omidria, which it sold to Rayner in 2021. Listed on Nasdaq (OMER). Revenue is limited and the company relies on equity raising and royalties, with about $1 billion raised in total per Crunchbase. Customers are hospitals and specialist physicians. B2B pharma with very little consumer brand awareness.

Prometheus Biosciences was a San Diego biotech developing precision treatments for inflammatory bowel disease, especially an antibody against TL1A for ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease, plus diagnostic tests for IBD. It listed on Nasdaq in 2021 and was acquired by Merck for about $10.8 billion in a deal announced in April 2023 and completed in June 2023, so it is now part of Merck. Crunchbase funding shows roughly $950 million. Customers were gastroenterologists and patients. It had no consumer brand awareness and no longer operates independently.

Terns Pharmaceuticals is a clinical-stage biotech in Foster City, California, developing oral small-molecule drugs for metabolic disease and cancer, including a GLP-1 receptor agonist for obesity and a BCR-ABL inhibitor for chronic myeloid leukaemia. It is listed on Nasdaq (TERN). It has no marketed product, so revenue is minimal and it funds operations through equity offerings, with Crunchbase showing about $1.1 billion raised in total. Future customers are patients via health systems. A B2B biotech with little consumer awareness, but exposure to the fast-growing obesity-drug theme.

Treeline Biosciences is a privately held biotech based in Watertown, Massachusetts, with research sites also in the US and Ireland, building small-molecule medicines for cancer, immunology and neurology through a portfolio of asset-focused companies. It was founded around 2018 and backed by large private investors, with roughly $1.1 billion raised in total per Crunchbase. It has no marketed product and earns revenue only through partnerships and funding. Customers would be patients and healthcare providers. A B2B drug-discovery company with no consumer brand awareness.

Wanda E-Commerce was the online commerce venture of Chinese conglomerate Dalian Wanda Group, based in Beijing, launched around 2014 to link Wanda's shopping malls and retail tenants with online shoppers and loyalty services, in partnership with Tencent and Baidu. Crunchbase shows a large CN¥6 billion round in January 2015. The business never became a major force against Alibaba and JD.com and was later wound down or folded into Wanda's other digital efforts. Consumer-facing in China only; no current brand profile outside the group.

AFI Europe Romania is the Romanian arm of AFI Europe, a real estate developer and investor with its business centred in Bucharest. It develops and operates office buildings, retail centres and residential projects, including large mixed-use schemes such as AFI Cotroceni and AFI Tech Park. Customers are tenants, retail shoppers and home buyers, and revenue comes from rents and sales. Crunchbase shows a financing of about 657 million in November 2025. Local property brand in Romania; no international consumer visibility.

Ayala Land is the Philippines' largest listed property developer, part of the Ayala conglomerate and based in Manila. It develops and manages master-planned communities, residential condominiums, office towers, shopping malls (such as Greenbelt and Glorietta in Makati), hotels and industrial parks, and sells under brands like Alveo, Avida and Amaia. Customers are Filipino home buyers, tenants, shoppers and businesses. Listed on the Philippine Stock Exchange (ALI), with annual revenue in the hundreds of billions of pesos. Very visible domestic consumer brand.

Beijing Weiying Technology is the operator of Maoyan Entertainment, China's leading online movie ticketing and entertainment platform, headquartered in Beijing. It sells cinema tickets via apps and WeChat, provides movie marketing and data services to studios, and has expanded into live events and film production and distribution. Consumers pay per ticket and studios pay for promotion. It is backed by Tencent, Meituan and others; Maoyan listed in Hong Kong in 2019 (stock code 1896). Crunchbase shows about $800 million raised. Strong consumer brand in China, with opportunities for entertainment and event tie-ins.

Djezzy is one of Algeria's three mobile network operators, based in Algiers, providing mobile voice, data, 4G and 5G services and mobile payments to tens of millions of subscribers. Customers are consumers and businesses, and revenue comes from airtime, data and enterprise services. It started as Orascom Telecom Algeria in 2001, was part of VimpelCom and later Veon, and in 2022 Veon sold a majority to the Algerian state-owned Fonds National d'Investissement. It is a household brand in Algeria and a major local sports sponsor.

Fenway Sports Group is a US sports, media and entertainment holding company based in Boston that owns the Boston Red Sox, Liverpool FC, the Pittsburgh Penguins (since 2021), a stake in RFK Racing in NASCAR and the sports marketing agency Fenway Sports Management, plus media assets like NESN. Revenue comes from ticketing, broadcasting, sponsorship, merchandising and marketing services. Owned by John W. Henry and partners, with RedBird Capital taking a minority stake in 2021 and other investors since. A major sports-business operator and a potential partner, intermediary or competitor for sponsorship dealings, with strong visibility.

MGM Growth Properties was a real estate investment trust created by MGM Resorts in 2016 to own the real estate of major Las Vegas and regional casino resorts, including Bellagio, MGM Grand and Mandalay Bay, and lease them back to MGM Resorts under long-term triple-net leases. Based in Las Vegas, it was listed on the NYSE (MGP). Customers were its tenant operators, and revenue was rent. Vici Properties acquired it in a deal completed in April 2022, so it no longer exists as an independent company. B2B landlord with little consumer brand awareness.

Vital Thin Film Materials (Guangdong) is a Shenzhen-area Chinese maker of high-purity sputtering targets and evaporation materials used in thin-film coating for displays, semiconductors, solar cells and optical applications. Customers are display, chip and component manufacturers, and revenue comes from material sales. It is a privately held company that has raised capital from investors, with Crunchbase showing about CN¥5.7 billion in funding and a round in September 2022. B2B industrial materials supplier with little consumer awareness, so a limited fit for brand sponsorship.

YIT is a Finnish construction and property development group headquartered in Helsinki. It builds and develops housing, business premises, hospitals and infrastructure, including roads, rail, bridges and urban areas, mostly in Finland, the Baltic countries and Central and Eastern Europe. Customers are home buyers, investors, municipalities and companies, and it earns revenue from sales and construction contracts. Listed on Nasdaq Helsinki (YIT) with revenue of around EUR 2 billion and several thousand employees; founded in 1912. Well-known domestic construction brand in Finland, with little consumer profile elsewhere.

Yoda PLC is described by Crunchbase as a Cyprus-listed investment company, based in Nicosia, Cyprus. No industries are shown, and only a short description is available. The input shows funding of about 743 million and a latest funding date of September 2026, which suggests it is a holding or investment vehicle rather than a consumer-facing operating business. There is no reliable information on its portfolio, owners, customers or products from the input. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Airtel Mobile Commerce BV is the mobile money operation of Airtel Africa, running Airtel Money services across about 14 African countries from its base in Nairobi, Kenya (the legal entity is Dutch). It offers wallets, transfers, bill payments, savings and merchant payments to tens of millions of mostly unbanked mobile users, and earns fees on transactions. It is a subsidiary of Airtel Africa (listed in London and Lagos), which is controlled by Bharti Airtel, and raised about $550 million from outside investors in 2021 (TPG, Mastercard). Airtel is a recognised consumer brand across Africa, with sports sponsorship history.

GreenSky was an Atlanta-based fintech that operated a point-of-sale lending platform letting merchants, mainly home-improvement contractors and healthcare providers, offer instant consumer loans through bank partners. It earned fees from merchants and banks rather than lending directly. It listed on Nasdaq in 2018 and was acquired by Goldman Sachs for about $2.2 billion in a deal announced in September 2021 and completed in 2022. Crunchbase shows $610 million raised. Consumers rarely knew the brand since it ran behind merchants, so low public awareness.

Hana Securities is a South Korean brokerage and investment bank headquartered in Seoul and a subsidiary of Hana Financial Group (formerly Hana Daetoo Securities, renamed in 2016). It offers stock brokerage, wealth management, investment banking, bond and derivatives trading, and asset management to retail and institutional clients, and earns commissions, fees and trading income. Hana Financial is listed in Seoul and is a major Korean financial group with a recognisable consumer brand through Hana Bank. Crunchbase shows about $600 million of recent financing.

Houzz is an online platform and app for home remodelling and interior design, started in 2009 and based in Palo Alto, California (listed in West Hollywood). Homeowners browse millions of photos, find professionals such as architects and contractors, and shop for furniture and decor, while Houzz earns revenue from advertising, a marketplace and SaaS tools for home professionals. Backed by investors including Sequoia, GGV and Comcast Ventures, with about $613 million raised. Well-known consumer-facing home brand in the US, UK and parts of Europe.

Khorlochhu Hydro Power is described in the input as a facility management company based in Thimphu, Bhutan, with Crunchbase industries listed as Construction and Facilities Support Services. The name indicates a hydropower project, probably a company connected to a run-of-river hydroelectric development on the Khorlochhu river in Bhutan, but the input does not confirm its owners, capacity or customers. Funding of about 56.6 billion is shown in an unspecified currency, with a latest date in September 2025. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

LS Digital is an Indian digital transformation and technology group based in Navi Mumbai, offering digital marketing, analytics, e-commerce, cloud and AI services to large enterprises. It earns fees from client projects and platform services and counts banks, telecoms and consumer brands as customers. Crunchbase shows about $611 million in funding, with a 2022 round that is reported to have valued the group at over a billion dollars. Privately held and growing through acquisitions. B2B agency and technology services brand with limited consumer awareness.

Superior Plus is a Toronto-based Canadian company, listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (SPB), that distributes propane and other energy products. Its main businesses are Superior Propane in Canada, propane distribution in the US and wholesale operations. Customers are households, farms and industrial clients that buy propane for heating, cooking and fuel. Revenue runs to roughly C$3 billion annually, with hundreds of thousands of customers. It is a dividend-paying income company, formed in 1996 as a trust. Regionally familiar energy brand, with little national consumer sponsorship profile.

TechMet is a critical-minerals investment company, headquartered in Dublin, that takes stakes in mining and processing projects for metals such as lithium, nickel, cobalt, tantalum, tin and rare earths. Customers are battery, electronics and defence supply chains, and it earns revenue through offtake and equity returns. It is backed by the US International Development Finance Corporation and private investors; Crunchbase shows about $550 million in funding. It emerged in the late 2010s and is privately held. B2B natural-resources investor with little consumer brand awareness.

Adani Transmission Step-One is a subsidiary vehicle of Adani Energy Solutions (formerly Adani Transmission), India's largest private-sector power transmission and distribution group, based in Ahmedabad, Gujarat. It owns and operates high-voltage transmission lines and substations and, through related entities, electricity distribution, earning regulated tariffs from state utilities. The Adani Group is a large Indian conglomerate in ports, energy, airports and infrastructure. Crunchbase shows a $500 million funding event in March 2026. The group brand is well known in India, but this entity is a financing vehicle without its own consumer profile.

Appalachian Community Capital is a US non-profit community development financial institution, headquartered in Christiansburg, Virginia, that raises capital and lends to local community lenders and small businesses across Appalachia. It focuses on affordable housing, small business loans, healthcare and rural development. Its customers are other community lenders, and it earns income from interest and fees. Funded by federal programs such as Treasury CDFI funds and by investors, with about $505 million in funding per Crunchbase. A mission-driven finance brand with low consumer awareness.

Asana Partners Strategic Partners is described by Crunchbase as a joint venture, based in Charlotte, North Carolina. No industries are shown. The name suggests a vehicle linked to Asana Partners, a Charlotte-based real estate investment firm known for acquiring and managing neighbourhood retail centres in the US, but the input does not confirm the partners or assets involved. Funding of $500 million is recorded in June 2026, which points to an investment fund or joint-venture capital commitment rather than an operating consumer business. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Axalta Coating Systems is a global coatings maker headquartered in Philadelphia, producing liquid and powder coatings for car refinish (Cromax, Standox, Spies Hecker brands), light vehicles, commercial vehicles and industrial applications. It was carved out of DuPont's performance coatings business in 2013, after Carlyle bought it. Customers are body shops, car makers and industrial manufacturers, and it has revenue of around $5 billion with roughly 12,000 employees and sales in about 130 countries. It is listed on the NYSE (AXTA). B2B brand with a long record in motorsport sponsorship, including NASCAR.

Babcock & Wilcox Enterprises is an Akron, Ohio, American energy technology and services company that makes boilers, steam generation equipment, environmental systems for emissions control and renewable and waste-to-energy plants, plus aftermarket services for power and industrial customers. Customers are utilities, industrial plants and governments worldwide. Listed on the NYSE (BW), it has revenue of several hundred million dollars, and its roots go back to 1867. It has been working on carbon capture and clean hydrogen technologies. A B2B industrial brand with limited consumer awareness.

Braskem Idesa is a Mexican petrochemical company, a joint venture between Brazil's Braskem (about 75 percent) and Mexican company Idesa (25 percent), based in Mexico City. It runs the Etileno XXI complex in Coatzacoalcos, Veracruz, producing polyethylene from ethane, including high-density and low-density grades, which it sells to plastic packaging and consumer-goods manufacturers in Mexico and abroad. Revenue is in the billions of dollars; it is financed with project-finance bonds. B2B industrial company with no consumer brand profile.

Burjeel Holdings is the largest private healthcare group in Abu Dhabi, founded by Dr Shamsheer Vayalil and part of VPS Healthcare. It operates hospitals, day-surgery centres, clinics and pharmacies in the UAE and Oman under Burjeel, Medeor, Lifecare and other brands, and earns money from patient and insurance payments. It listed on the Abu Dhabi Securities Exchange (BURJEEL) in October 2022, with annual revenue near AED 5 billion. Strong regional consumer healthcare brand in the Gulf, with a high-income customer base.

Collinson Group is a London-based customer loyalty and travel services business that runs airport lounge access through Priority Pass, plus travel insurance, flight-delay compensation, digital rewards and loyalty programmes for banks, airlines and card issuers. Customers are mainly financial institutions and travel brands that bundle benefits for their cardholders; consumers use Priority Pass lounges in over 150 countries. It is privately owned, and Crunchbase shows about 350 million of investment in September 2026. Priority Pass is a well-known premium traveller brand with an affluent audience.

Copper World is a copper mining project in Arizona near Tucson, developed by Hudbay Minerals (Toronto-listed, TSX and NYSE: HBM) near its Rosemont area. It plans an open-pit copper operation with a processing plant, with moly and silver by-products, and aims to supply the growing copper demand for electrification. A joint-venture partner was brought in to fund part of the build, so the funding figure shown reflects project financing. B2B resources project with no consumer brand profile and little relevance for brand sponsorship.

Datapipe was a managed hosting and cloud services provider founded in 1996 and based in Jersey City, New Jersey, that ran data centres and managed IT infrastructure on public cloud platforms such as Amazon Web Services and Microsoft Azure for large enterprises. It earned recurring fees from managed services contracts. Backed by private equity, it was acquired by Rackspace in 2017, so it no longer operates as an independent company. B2B IT services brand with little consumer awareness.

Distalmotion is a Swiss medical device company, based in Epalinges near Lausanne, that makes the Dexter robotic surgical system, a more modular and compact robot for minimally invasive surgery in urology, gynaecology and general surgery. It sells systems and single-use instruments to hospitals and ambulatory surgery centres in Europe and the US. It is private and venture-backed, having raised over $450 million including a major recent round. It competes with Intuitive Surgical's da Vinci. B2B medical technology brand with low consumer awareness.

EcoCeres is a Hong Kong-headquartered producer of sustainable and renewable fuels, converting used cooking oil and other biomass waste into biodiesel and sustainable aviation fuel, with plants in China and Malaysia. Customers are airlines, fuel traders and industrial clients, mainly in Europe, and it earns revenue from fuel sales. In 2023 it raised about $500 million from institutional investors, giving it roughly $508 million in Crunchbase funding. Private company; B2B and little consumer awareness, though sustainable aviation fuel is of growing interest to airlines and motorsport.

Everpure appears to be the new name of Pure Storage, the Santa Clara, California maker of all-flash enterprise data storage systems, including FlashArray and FlashBlade, plus the Evergreen subscription model and Portworx cloud-native storage. Customers are large enterprises, cloud providers and AI data centres buying hardware and subscriptions. Pure Storage listed on the NYSE (PSTG) in 2015 and has revenue near $3 billion. The $529 million shown reflects pre-IPO funding up to 2014. B2B technology brand with modest consumer awareness.

G4S was a London-based global security services group offering manned guarding, cash handling, secure facilities management, alarm monitoring and prisoner custody services in around 85 countries, with about 800,000 employees at its peak. Customers were governments, banks, retailers and corporates. It was listed on the London Stock Exchange before being acquired in 2021 by US firm Allied Universal for about GBP 3.8 billion, so it now operates as part of Allied Universal. Familiar B2B and public-sector brand, also known as a sports sponsor.

Good Technology was a Sunnyvale, California mobile security and enterprise mobility software company known for secure email and application containers (Good for Enterprise) that let employees use personal phones for work. Customers were large corporates, government agencies and financial institutions paying subscriptions. It was acquired by BlackBerry in 2015 for about $425 million, and its products were folded into BlackBerry's enterprise portfolio. Crunchbase shows about $479 million raised in total. B2B software brand with no ongoing independent existence and little consumer awareness.

Hundsun Technologies is a Hangzhou-based Chinese financial software and services group, supplying trading, securities, asset management, fund and bank systems to brokers, banks, asset managers and exchanges across China. It earns licence, maintenance and services revenue. Listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange (600570), it is a leading domestic fintech supplier, with Ant Group as a major shareholder, and employs several thousand staff. B2B brand with little consumer awareness.

Konecranes is a Finnish industrial group headquartered in Hyvinkaa that makes overhead cranes, hoists, port cranes and lift trucks, and services lifting equipment in ports, factories, shipyards and other industries worldwide. Customers are manufacturers, ports and logistics firms, and it earns money from equipment sales and recurring maintenance contracts. It is listed on Nasdaq Helsinki (KCR), has about 16,000 employees and revenue of around EUR 4 billion. B2B industrial brand with strong presence in ports and heavy industry, and little consumer awareness.

Lithium Argentina (formerly Lithium Americas (Argentina)) is a Vancouver-based mining company, listed on the TSX and NYSE, which holds interests in lithium brine projects in Argentina's lithium triangle, including Caucharí-Olaroz (a joint venture with Ganfeng Lithium and JEMSE) and the Pastos Grandes basin. It sells lithium carbonate to battery and electric-vehicle supply chains. It was spun out of Lithium Americas in 2023 after the split from the Thacker Pass project. Customers are battery makers, and revenue depends on lithium prices. B2B resources brand with little consumer awareness.

Livin Housing is a social housing provider and non-profit organisation based in Spennymoor, County Durham, England, managing and building affordable homes for rent and shared ownership across County Durham and Teesside. It is a housing association serving tens of thousands of tenants. Revenue comes from rents and grants, and it borrows from lenders; Crunchbase shows about 350 million in funding in August 2026. Regional charity-like housing brand with little national consumer awareness, so a limited fit for global sponsorship.

LSI Industries is a Cincinnati, Ohio, manufacturer of commercial lighting and display solutions, including LED lighting for petrol stations, car dealerships, parking and sports venues, plus retail display fixtures, digital signage and graphics for major retail and convenience chains. Customers are large retailers, oil companies, restaurant chains and facility owners, and it earns revenue from product sales and installation programmes. Listed on Nasdaq (LYTS), with revenue of roughly $500 million. Founded in 1976. B2B brand with little consumer awareness.

National HealthCare Corporation (NHC) operates senior care facilities in the United States from its Murfreesboro, Tennessee base, including skilled nursing homes, assisted and independent living communities, memory care and home health and hospice services, mainly in the south-eastern US. Residents, families, Medicare and Medicaid pay for care. It is listed on the NYSE American (NHC), has several dozen facilities and thousands of employees, and was founded in 1971. Regional healthcare brand with limited national consumer awareness.

OASIS Holding Company is a Kuwaiti investment company, described as incorporated in 2008 and active in financial services and venture investing, based in Fahaheel, Kuwait. It invests in a range of businesses through direct holdings and ventures, and revenue comes from investment returns and subsidiaries. Crunchbase shows about $520 million of funding in 2018. Little else is confirmed in the input. Regional investment brand with a limited public profile; potentially relevant as a Gulf-based financial holding group. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Omada Health is a San Francisco digital health company that offers virtual chronic-condition care programmes for diabetes prevention, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, musculoskeletal pain and weight management, including GLP-1 support. Members get coaching, connected devices (scales, glucose meters) and app-based support, paid for by employers, health plans and government programmes. Founded in 2011, it listed on Nasdaq (OMDA) in June 2025. Crunchbase shows about $540 million raised pre-IPO. B2B2C health brand reaching hundreds of thousands of members, with moderate public awareness.

Pandora is a Danish jewellery maker and retailer based in Copenhagen, best known for its charm bracelets and rings, and increasingly lab-grown diamond jewellery. It designs and manufactures in Thailand and sells through thousands of points of sale, including around 2,700 concept stores, in about 100 countries, with revenue of roughly DKK 28-30 billion. Customers are mainly women buying gifts and self-purchases. Listed on Nasdaq Copenhagen (PNDORA), founded in 1982. Very recognisable consumer brand with global reach and heavy marketing spend.

Plastic Logic Germany is the Dresden-based operation of Plastic Logic, a company that developed flexible plastic electronics and organic thin-film transistor displays, including e-paper screens and lightweight e-reader devices. It set up a factory in Dresden around 2008-2010 and had raised about $500 million from investors including Oak Investment Partners and Russian group Rusnano. The Que e-reader was cancelled before launch in 2010 and the business was later restructured, with the Dresden unit continuing as a display technology supplier. Limited consumer brand visibility; much of the story is historic.

RecNation Storage is a family-run self-storage operator based in Wylie, Texas, focused on recreational vehicle, boat and vehicle storage, with outdoor, covered and enclosed spaces alongside conventional units. Customers are RV, boat and car owners and households, and it earns monthly rental fees. Crunchbase shows a $500 million financing in May 2023, which suggests a large property-acquisition funding. It operates a growing portfolio of facilities in the southern and central US. Regional consumer storage brand with little national awareness.

Silvercorp Metals is a Vancouver-based precious and base metals miner that operates silver-lead-zinc mines in China (the Ying district in Henan and the GC mine in Guangdong), and has expanded into gold with the Condor project in Ecuador. It sells concentrates to Chinese smelters and earns revenue of around $200-300 million. Listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange and NYSE American (SVM). Founded in 2004. B2B resources company with limited consumer brand awareness.

Sogou was a Chinese internet company headquartered in Beijing, best known for its Pinyin input method and its search engine, which earned money from advertising, search and AI-based voice and translation products. It was controlled by Sohu and backed by Tencent, which owned a significant stake. Sogou listed on the NYSE (SOGO) in 2017 and was taken private by Tencent in 2021, being absorbed into Tencent's search business. Crunchbase shows about $516 million raised, and the brand was widely known in China, but it no longer operates independently.

Svante is a Burnaby, British Columbia, cleantech company that develops solid sorbent carbon capture filters (using metal-organic frameworks) and builds modular systems that capture CO2 from cement, steel, hydrogen and power plants. Customers are industrial emitters, and it earns revenue from equipment, filters and technology licences, backed by large investors including Chevron and Temasek. Crunchbase shows about $510 million in funding. Privately held, founded in 2007 as Inventys. B2B climate-technology brand with limited consumer visibility, though it features in industrial decarbonisation discussions.

Tetra Tech is a Pasadena, California consulting and engineering firm focused on water, environment, infrastructure, resource management and energy, serving US federal, state and municipal governments, utilities and commercial clients across North America, Australia and the UK. It earns revenue from project and services contracts, around $5 billion annually with about 28,000 staff. Listed on Nasdaq (TTEK), founded in 1966. Government and utilities supplier with strong B2B reputation and little consumer brand awareness.

United Imaging Healthcare is a Shanghai-based medical imaging and radiotherapy equipment maker producing MRI, CT, PET/CT, X-ray and ultrasound systems and radiotherapy equipment, sold to hospitals in China and increasingly overseas. Customers are hospitals and clinics, and revenue comes from equipment sales and service. It is a leading domestic competitor to GE, Siemens and Philips, and listed on the Shanghai STAR Market (688271) in 2022. Founded in 2011. B2B medical technology brand, mainly known within healthcare; limited consumer awareness.

Vireo Growth (formerly Goodness Growth Holdings and Vireo Health) is a Minneapolis-based multi-state cannabis operator that cultivates, processes and sells cannabis products through its own dispensaries and wholesale channels, including Green Goods retail stores. Operations include Minnesota, New York, Maryland, Arizona and other US states. Customers are medical and adult-use cannabis consumers. It is listed on the Canadian Securities Exchange (VREO) and trades over the counter in the US. Crunchbase shows about $480 million raised. Cannabis restrictions limit mainstream advertising and sponsorship options.

WhiteHawk Minerals is described by Crunchbase as an investment company based in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, operating in the energy and energy efficiency sectors. The name suggests it holds mineral and royalty interests, but the input does not confirm its products, owners or scale. Crunchbase shows a funding figure of about $524 million in September 2026, which points to an investment vehicle rather than a consumer-facing operating business. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Battelle Memorial Institute is a non-profit applied science and technology organisation based in Columbus, Ohio, running contract research for the US government and industry in areas such as national security, health, energy, advanced materials and cybersecurity. It manages or co-manages several US national laboratories, including Pacific Northwest National Laboratory, and has thousands of employees. Founded in 1929 from the will of industrialist Gordon Battelle; it developed xerography with Haloid. B2B and government research institute with little consumer brand awareness.

Elevra Lithium is the Brisbane-based lithium miner formed in 2025 from the merger of Sayona Mining and Piedmont Lithium, with assets in Quebec, Canada (the North American Lithium operation) and projects in the US. It produces spodumene concentrate for battery makers, with revenue dependent on lithium prices. It is listed in Australia on the ASX and in the US on Nasdaq. Customers include battery and chemical converters. B2B natural-resources company with no consumer profile.

Frontier Energy is a Perth, Western Australia based company developing renewable energy projects, notably the Waroona solar and battery project in Western Australia, and earlier tied to mineral and solar assets. Customers would be electricity retailers and industrial users buying power under offtake agreements. It is listed on the ASX (FHE). The input shows a funding figure of about A$614 million, likely reflecting project-related financing. Small-cap B2B energy developer with no consumer awareness.

Ganfeng Lithium is a Chinese lithium producer based in Xinyu, Jiangxi, producing lithium compounds and metal for batteries, with mining interests in Australia (Mt Marion), Argentina (Cauchari-Olaroz), Mali and Mexico. Customers include battery and electric-vehicle supply chains, and it also operates a solid-state battery and recycling business. Listed in Shenzhen (002460) and Hong Kong (1772), founded in 2000. Revenue is in the billions of yuan. B2B industrial brand, little consumer awareness.

Gimlet Labs is a San Francisco start-up building infrastructure software for running AI workloads across heterogeneous hardware, helping companies run models more efficiently across different chips and data centres. Customers are AI developers and enterprises. It raised about $392 million in total according to Crunchbase, with a large round around September 2026. Private, venture-backed. B2B developer brand with no consumer awareness. The details here come mostly from the Crunchbase description, so verify before outreach.

Go1 is a Brisbane-based online training content marketplace that aggregates corporate learning content, such as compliance, safety and leadership courses, from many providers and sells it to businesses, governments and training organisations through a single platform. Customers are employers and learning providers; it earns subscription and content revenue. Founded in 2015, it became an Australian unicorn after raising capital from investors including SoftBank Vision Fund and Salesforce Ventures, with about $400 million raised. B2B brand with little consumer awareness.

Gold Royalty Corp is a Vancouver-based precious metals royalty and streaming company that acquires royalties and streams on gold mines and projects, mainly in the Americas, earning revenue as a percentage of production without operating mines itself. Customers are mining companies who receive upfront funding. Listed on the NYSE American (GROY), it was founded in 2020 and IPO'd in 2021. Revenue is in the tens of millions of dollars. B2B finance brand with little consumer awareness.

Greenalia is a Spanish renewable energy company based in A Coruna, Galicia, developing and operating wind, solar and biomass power plants in Spain, Portugal, the US and Poland, and acting as an independent power producer. Customers are electricity buyers under power purchase agreements and the grid. Founded in 2011, it listed on the Spanish BME Growth market and continues to expand its pipeline. Crunchbase shows about $430 million in funding. Regional energy brand in northwest Spain, with limited consumer awareness.

Halio is a Hayward, California maker of electronically tintable smart glass for commercial buildings, formerly known as Kinestral Technologies. Its glass changes tint on demand to control heat and glare and is sold to building owners, architects and developers. Founded in 2012, it has raised about $400 million from investors including Corning. Crunchbase shows about $399 million. B2B construction-technology brand with little consumer awareness.

InflaRx is a German biotech based in Jena, developing complement-inhibiting antibody drugs for inflammatory diseases. Its anti-C5a antibody vilobelimab received emergency use authorisation in the US for severe Covid-19 and is being studied in skin diseases such as pyoderma gangrenosum, while an oral C5aR inhibitor is also in development. It has been listed on Nasdaq (IFRX) since 2017. Customers are hospitals and pharma partners. Revenue is small and it relies on equity raising, with about $437 million raised. B2B biotech with no consumer awareness.

ION Investment Group is a financial technology and data company headquartered in Dublin, founded by Andrea Pignataro, that provides trading, treasury, workflow, analytics and risk software to banks, hedge funds, corporates and central banks. It has grown mostly through acquisitions, including Fidessa, Dealogic and Acuris, and has thousands of staff worldwide. Privately owned, with revenue in the billions of dollars and large debt financing. B2B brand with little consumer awareness; it is a very large, wealthy financial-software group.

Kestra Medical Technologies is a Kirkland, Washington medical device company that makes the ASSURE wearable cardioverter defibrillator, a vest-like device that monitors heart rhythm and delivers a shock to patients at risk of sudden cardiac arrest, plus a remote-monitoring service. Customers are patients prescribed the device by cardiologists, with revenue from insurers. Listed on Nasdaq (KMTS) following an IPO in 2025. Competes with Zoll LifeVest. Crunchbase shows about $409 million raised. Healthcare B2B brand with low consumer awareness.

Liberty Global is an international cable and broadband group, registered in Bermuda with its headquarters in London, controlling or co-owning brands such as Virgin Media O2 in the UK (a joint venture with Telefonica), Telenet in Belgium, Sunrise in Switzerland and VodafoneZiggo in the Netherlands (a joint venture with Vodafone). Customers are consumers and businesses buying broadband, TV, mobile and telephony. Listed on Nasdaq (LBTYA, LBTYB, LBTYK). Founded by John Malone. Its operating brands are very recognisable and active in sports sponsorship.

Musely is a Santa Clara, California based prescription wellness and telehealth company offering custom-compounded dermatology products for hyperpigmentation, acne and ageing, and prescription weight-loss and women's health treatments, sold direct to consumers online with remote doctor consultations. Customers are mostly women buying skincare and wellness online, and revenue comes from product subscriptions. It is privately held, with about $388 million shown in funding in May 2026. Direct-to-consumer health brand marketed heavily online.

New Hope Group is an Australian energy company, headquartered in Brisbane and shown here with a Victoria address, that mines and sells thermal coal from the New Acland and Bengalla operations to power generators in Asia and Australia, and has interests in oil and gas and investments in renewable energy. Listed on the ASX (NHC), it had revenue of around A$1.5-2 billion. Customers are utilities and industrial buyers. It is controlled by the Washington H. Soul Pattinson group. B2B resources company with little consumer visibility.

Nuveen Churchill Direct Lending Corp is a US business development company that makes senior secured loans to private-equity-backed middle-market companies, managed by Churchill Asset Management, an affiliate of Nuveen and TIAA. Based in New York, it earns interest income on a loan portfolio of several billion dollars and is listed on the NYSE (NCDL) following a 2024 IPO. Customers are mid-sized US companies and investors. Finance B2B brand with no consumer awareness.

Nyxoah is a Belgian medical device company based in Mont-Saint-Guibert that makes the Genio system, a neurostimulation implant for obstructive sleep apnea that treats the condition by stimulating the hypoglossal nerve. It sells in Europe and received US FDA approval in 2025. Customers are sleep physicians, surgeons and patients, and revenue is growing but small. Listed on Nasdaq (NYXH), IPO in 2021. Competes with Inspire Medical. B2B medtech with limited consumer awareness.

Pan American Energy Corp is a Calgary, Alberta based junior exploration company, listed on the Canadian Securities Exchange, focused on mineral exploration, with projects in lithium and copper in the Americas. It is at an early stage, with no significant revenue. The Crunchbase funding figure of about $402 million appears large for an exploration-stage company and may reflect a transaction value. Not to be confused with the large Argentine oil company Pan American Energy. B2B resource explorer with no consumer awareness.

Phoenix Kallang is a joint venture involving Frasers Property, based in Singapore, developing a residential project in the Kallang area of Singapore. Frasers Property is a Singapore-listed property group with retail, residential, hospitality and industrial assets worldwide. The joint venture would earn revenue from selling apartments to home buyers. Crunchbase shows S$588 million of financing in July 2026, which suggests a land purchase or construction loan. Property project with little standalone brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Precision Neuroscience is a New York-based neurotechnology company building a brain-computer interface called the Layer 7 Cortical Interface, a very thin electrode film that sits on the brain's surface and can record and stimulate neural activity. It has FDA 510(k) clearance for short-term use and aims to help paralysed patients control computers. Founded in 2021 by Neuralink co-founder Ben Rapoport, it is privately held and has raised about $405 million. Customers are hospitals, neurosurgeons and researchers. High-profile frontier-tech brand but not yet a consumer product.

Rightway is a New York health technology company that provides pharmacy benefit management (PBM) and navigation tools to employers and health plans, with a focus on transparency, a member app, and clinical support for prescriptions and care. Customers are self-insured employers and health plans, and revenue comes from administrative fees and rebates. Founded in 2016, it has raised about $394 million from investors such as Founders Fund and Tiger Global. Private B2B2C brand with limited awareness among employees of client firms.

Shanghai Putailai New Energy Technology is a Chinese maker of lithium-ion battery materials, especially graphite anode materials, as well as separators, binders and coated films for battery cells. Customers are major battery producers such as CATL, LG and BYD, and it earns revenue from material sales. Headquartered in Shanghai, it is listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange and is one of the leading anode makers in the world, with Crunchbase showing about CN¥2.8 billion raised in 2023. B2B industrial brand with no consumer awareness.

Silvr is a French fintech, based in Neuilly-sur-Seine near Paris, offering revenue-based financing to online businesses, e-commerce brands and software firms, repaid as a share of future revenue instead of a traditional loan. Customers are small and mid-sized digital companies in France, the UK, Germany and other European markets. It was founded in 2020, and raised about EUR 363 million in funding including debt facilities. Privately held. B2B finance brand with limited consumer awareness.

Sunrise Energy Metals is a Melbourne-based Australian company that holds the Syerston nickel-cobalt-scandium project in New South Wales, positioning itself as a producer of high-purity metals for batteries and advanced technology. It is listed on the ASX (SRL), was previously Clean TeQ Holdings, and has no major revenue yet. Customers would be battery and aerospace materials buyers. B2B resources developer with no consumer profile.

Talkiatry is a New York-based virtual psychiatry practice offering mental health care through video visits with board-certified psychiatrists, covered by health insurance, for conditions such as depression, anxiety, ADHD and bipolar disorder. Patients book online, and revenue comes from insurance reimbursements. Founded in 2020, it operates across a large number of US states and has raised about $450 million from investors including General Catalyst and Tiger Global. Direct-to-consumer digital health brand with growing awareness through online and advertising campaigns.

Teck Resources is a Vancouver-based diversified mining company producing copper, zinc and steelmaking coal, with major mines in Canada, Chile and Peru including Highland Valley Copper, Quebrada Blanca and Red Dog. In 2024 it sold its steelmaking coal business to Glencore, and in 2025 it agreed to merge with Anglo American, creating Anglo Teck. Customers are smelters, steel mills and industrial buyers; annual revenue is around C$10 billion. Listed on the TSX and NYSE (TECK). B2B resource brand with limited consumer awareness.

Thyme Care is a Nashville-based healthcare company providing value-based cancer care management for health plans, using nurses, navigators and technology to support patients and oncologists and cut avoidable emergency visits. Customers are insurers and cancer practices, and it earns revenue from care-management fees and shared savings. Founded in 2020 by former Flatiron Health executives, it has raised about $400 million from investors such as General Catalyst and Lead Edge. B2B healthcare brand with little consumer awareness.

VMware is a Palo Alto, California virtualisation and cloud infrastructure software company known for vSphere, vCenter, NSX and the VMware Cloud platform, serving large enterprises, governments and service providers. It earns licence, subscription and support revenue. It was founded in 1998, owned for years by EMC then Dell, spun off in 2021, and acquired by Broadcom for about $69 billion in November 2023. Crunchbase's $393 million funding reflects 2007 funding. Strong B2B technology brand, now part of Broadcom and no longer independent.

Westgold Resources is a Perth, Western Australia gold producer that operates several mines and processing hubs in the Murchison and Southern Goldfields regions of Western Australia, producing roughly 250,000-300,000 ounces of gold per year. It sells gold bullion into the market and has acquired assets including the Great Southern and Karora operations. Listed on the ASX (WGX), founded in 2013. B2B resources producer with no consumer awareness.

Xreal is a Beijing-based maker of augmented reality glasses, formerly Nreal, selling consumer AR display glasses such as Xreal Air, Air 2 and One that plug into phones, laptops and consoles to show a large virtual screen, as well as the Beam accessory. Customers are consumers, gamers and travellers, and revenue is from hardware sales in Asia, North America and Europe. Founded in 2017, it has raised about $450 million from investors including Alibaba and iQiyi. Growing consumer tech brand with a strong online presence.

Xunlei is a Shenzhen-based Chinese internet company best known for its download accelerator and peer-to-peer file-sharing software, which has since moved into shared cloud computing, blockchain-related services and subscription products for consumers and businesses. It earns revenue from subscriptions, cloud computing and live-streaming. Listed on Nasdaq (XNET) since 2014, with about $420 million of private funding shown in Crunchbase. Founded in 2003. Well-known tech brand in China but with limited global awareness.

WELL Health Technologies is a Vancouver-based Canadian digital health company that owns and operates primary care clinics, a virtual care business, electronic medical record software (including OSCAR), and a growing digital healthcare services arm with US and international acquisitions. Customers are patients, physicians and health systems; revenue is over C$1 billion. Listed on the TSX (WELL), founded in 2010. Regional healthcare brand with moderate consumer visibility in Canada, and the owner of well-known clinic networks.

Sage is listed in the input as a New York company in business intelligence and eldercare-related industries, with a short description about an operational management system used by care providers. The input does not make clear whether this is a senior-care technology start-up or another firm called Sage, so it should not be confused with the British accounting software group Sage Group plc. Crunchbase shows about $159 million of funding in July 2026. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

AppDynamics was a San Francisco-based application performance management software company that monitored the health of enterprise software and web applications, linking IT performance to business metrics for large companies and banks. Customers were enterprises that paid subscription fees. Founded in 2008, it raised about $364 million and was acquired by Cisco in January 2017 for about $3.7 billion, just before its planned IPO; it now operates as part of Cisco. B2B technology brand with limited consumer awareness.

Applus Services is a Madrid-based global testing, inspection and certification company with around 25,000 employees, offering technical inspections and certification for energy, infrastructure, automotive and aerospace clients, and vehicle inspection programmes in several countries. Customers are industrial firms, governments and car owners, and it earns service revenue of roughly EUR 2 billion. It was listed on the Madrid stock exchange before being taken private by a private equity-backed bidder in 2024. Its Idiada unit is also known in automotive testing and motorsport. B2B brand.

Chinac.com is a Xiamen-based Chinese cloud computing provider offering domain registration, web hosting, cloud servers and managed cloud services to small and medium businesses in China. Customers are SMEs and developers, and it earns subscription and usage revenue. It has raised about $379 million of investment according to Crunchbase, including a significant 2018 round. Smaller domestic competitor to Alibaba Cloud and Tencent Cloud. B2B technology brand with limited consumer awareness.

Cypherpunk Technologies, based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, is understood to be the renamed former clinical-stage cancer biotech Leap Therapeutics, which in 2025 pivoted to a corporate treasury strategy built around the privacy-focused cryptocurrency Zcash. Crunchbase still lists it as a biopharmaceutical and fintech company, with about $359 million in total funding recorded. It is listed on Nasdaq and earns no material product revenue. Customers and products are unclear after the pivot. Little consumer brand awareness beyond crypto investors; verify before outreach.

Fab.com was a New York-based online design retailer and flash-sale marketplace selling furniture, home decor, gadgets and gifts at a discount, started as a gay social network in 2010 and pivoted to design products. It raised over $330 million from investors including Andreessen Horowitz and Menlo Ventures, expanded to Europe through acquisitions, but burned cash and shrank sharply in 2013-14. Its brand and assets were sold to PCH International in 2015 and it no longer operates as before. Briefly well known to design-minded consumers.

GitHub is a San Francisco developer platform for hosting code and collaborating on software projects, with over 100 million developers. It sells GitHub Enterprise, Actions, Copilot (its AI coding assistant) and security tools through subscriptions to individuals, teams and large enterprises. Founded in 2008, it was acquired by Microsoft in 2018 for $7.5 billion and operates as a Microsoft subsidiary. Crunchbase shows $350 million raised in 2015. Strong developer brand with a big tech-community profile, but B2B-focused.

GTA (GTA Teleguam) is the main telecommunications provider in Guam, based in Hagatna, offering mobile, broadband internet, TV and landline services to residents and businesses in Guam and the Northern Mariana Islands, with subsea cable connectivity. It has a long operating history as a local carrier. Crunchbase shows about $346 million in financing in 2023, likely for network expansion. A well-known local brand in Guam with community-level sponsorships, but small global reach.

Instalco is a Stockholm-based technical installation group that installs and services heating, ventilation, plumbing, electrical, cooling and automation systems for housing, industry and public buildings, with operations in Sweden, Norway, Finland and Denmark, built through acquisitions of many local firms. Customers are property owners, municipalities and industry; revenue is about SEK 15 billion. Listed on Nasdaq Stockholm (INSTAL), founded in 2014. B2B contractor with low public brand awareness, though a large employer in the Nordic region.

Kakao Pay is a South Korean fintech affiliate of Kakao Corp, based in Seongnam, operating the KakaoPay payments and wallet app, with services in money transfer, online and offline payments, credit scoring, insurance, investment and loans for tens of millions of users. Revenue comes from payment fees and financial products. Listed on the KOSDAQ since 2021, with Ant Group as a major shareholder. Strong consumer app brand in Korea, tied to the KakaoTalk messaging ecosystem.

LiftForward was a New York-based financial services company that provided payment solutions and working capital to small businesses, with repayments that flexed with sales. Crunchbase shows about $366 million in total funding, with a November 2016 date, which likely includes a debt facility. The input does not confirm its later history, owners or whether it still operates. B2B small business finance brand with limited consumer awareness. Details beyond the Crunchbase description are not confirmed here. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Luz Saude is one of the largest private healthcare groups in Portugal, headquartered in Lisbon, operating the Hospital da Luz network of private hospitals, clinics and senior care residences, and offering emergency, surgery, maternity and diagnostics. Patients and insurers pay for care. It is owned by Fidelidade, the Portuguese insurer which is itself majority-owned by Chinese group Fosun, and has around 10 hospitals and thousands of staff. Crunchbase shows about 310 million of funding in September 2025. Strong healthcare brand in Portugal.

Nynas is a Stockholm-based specialist oil refiner producing naphthenic oils, such as transformer oils, process oils and bitumen products for road paving, used by electrical equipment makers, tyre and rubber producers and construction. It operates refineries in Sweden, the UK, Belgium and Germany, sells in many countries, and is known in the Nordics. Ownership has included Neste and Petroleos de Venezuela, and Nynas went through a restructuring in 2022 with creditors becoming owners. B2B industrial brand with little consumer awareness.

Qualitas Group is a Melbourne-based real estate investment manager, listed on the ASX (QAL) since 2021, that manages funds and property investments in build-to-rent, residential, commercial and credit, with about A$5 billion under management. It earns management fees, performance fees and returns from its own balance sheet. Customers are institutional and wholesale investors, and it has developed projects across Australian cities. Founded in 2008. B2B finance brand with little consumer awareness.

Silicor Materials was a solar-grade silicon producer that developed a low-cost aluminium-alloy process for making polysilicon for solar cells, with a planned plant in Iceland, and raised roughly $345 million. The input places it in Berlin, Germany, while the company was better known in the US (San Jose) and was previously called Calisolar. The Icelandic project ran into financing difficulties and the company stopped operating before delivering the plant. Historic B2B solar-materials brand; no ongoing consumer profile.

Sumo Logic is a Redwood City, California cloud-based log management, security analytics and observability platform used by DevOps and security teams to monitor applications and detect threats. Customers are software-driven enterprises paying subscriptions. Founded in 2010, it listed on Nasdaq (SUMO) in 2020 and was taken private by Francisco Partners in 2023 for about $1.7 billion. Crunchbase shows about $340 million raised before its IPO. B2B technology brand with little consumer awareness.

Synthomer is a London-headquartered specialty chemicals company making polymers and ingredients, such as latex for nitrile gloves, adhesives, coatings, construction chemicals, and performance materials, with plants in Europe, Asia and North America. Customers are manufacturers of gloves, paints, adhesives and building products. Listed on the London Stock Exchange (SYNT), with revenue around GBP 2 billion, and with roots in the Yule Catto group. B2B industrial brand with minimal consumer awareness.

Tuandaiwang was a Chinese peer-to-peer lending platform based in Dongguan, Guangdong, which connected individual investors with borrowers, run by Tuandai Financial. It raised about CN¥2.4 billion in a 2017 funding round and grew into one of the larger platforms until Chinese regulators cracked down on P2P lending in 2018-2019, after which it ran into legal trouble. The business is defunct. Past domestic consumer finance brand in China only.

VACUUMSCHMELZE (VAC) is a German advanced materials company, based in Hanau, that makes magnetic materials and components, including soft-magnetic alloys, rare-earth permanent magnets, and parts for electric motors, sensors, transformers and electric vehicles. Customers are car makers, electronics and industrial firms. Founded in 1914, it has about 5,000 employees and a global footprint, with a US magnet plant in South Carolina. Crunchbase records a $335 million financing in September 2024. B2B industrial brand with little consumer awareness.

Weidian is a Beijing-based Chinese mobile e-commerce platform that lets individuals and small merchants set up online shops on their phones and sell through social channels, often through WeChat, with tools for payments, logistics and marketing. It also launched the Weidian app for consumers. Founded in 2011, with funding from investors including Sequoia and Tencent, and about $368 million raised in total. Domestic consumer and SME platform, moderately well-known in China.

ZTE Microelectronics Technology (ZTE Microelectronics, also called Sanechips) is the chip design subsidiary of Chinese telecom equipment maker ZTE, based in Shenzhen, designing semiconductors for communications networks, consumer devices, automotive and IoT. Customers are mostly ZTE and other equipment makers. It raised capital from outside investors, with about $376 million raised in 2015. Part of the ZTE group, which is listed in Shenzhen and Hong Kong. B2B semiconductor brand with no consumer awareness.

Aareon is a Mainz-based European software and services provider for the property and housing industry, with its Aareon Smart Platform and products such as Wodis Yuneo and tenant engagement tools, selling to housing associations, property managers and landlords in Germany, the Netherlands, the UK, France and Scandinavia. Revenue is in the hundreds of millions of euros. It is owned by Advent International with Aareal Bank group also involved, and TPG joined as a co-investor in 2024. B2B real estate technology brand, little consumer awareness.

AccessOne is a Fort Mill, South Carolina company that offers patient financing and payment plans for medical bills, helping hospitals and health systems offer interest-free instalments to patients while receiving funds quickly. Customers are healthcare providers, and it earns fees and finance income. Founded in 2001, Crunchbase records a $300 million financing in 2019. B2B healthcare finance brand with little consumer awareness beyond patients, and no consumer-facing marketing profile to speak of.

Anaplan is a business planning software company, founded in San Francisco and shown with a Miami address in the input, that sells a cloud platform for connected planning across finance, sales, supply chain and workforce. Customers are large enterprises paying subscriptions. Founded in 2006, it listed on the NYSE (PLAN) in 2018 and was taken private by Thoma Bravo for about $10.7 billion in 2022. Crunchbase shows about $300 million raised in 2018. B2B software brand with little consumer awareness.

Barnes & Noble is the largest bookstore chain in the United States, headquartered in New York, operating around 600 stores selling books, toys, games, gifts and music, and its online store and Nook e-reader business. Customers are consumers, and it earns revenue from retail sales and memberships. It was acquired by hedge fund Elliott Advisors in 2019 and is run by James Daunt, who also leads Waterstones. Crunchbase shows a $300 million investment from Microsoft in 2012. A very well-known consumer brand in the US, with a loyal customer base.

BenevolentAI is a London-based clinical-stage AI-enabled drug discovery company, which uses its platform to analyse biomedical data and find new drug targets for diseases such as atopic dermatitis and ulcerative colitis, in partnership with AstraZeneca and others. It raised around $290 million privately before listing in Amsterdam in 2022 via a SPAC merger. In 2025 it was taken private by its largest shareholder after cutting back sharply. B2B biotech with some recognition in life sciences, but little consumer awareness.

Cylance was an AI-driven endpoint security company, originally based in Irvine, California, that used machine learning to detect malware and threats on computers for enterprise and government customers. The input location is Eden Prairie, Minnesota, but its main base was California. Founded in 2012, it raised about $297 million and was acquired by BlackBerry in 2019 for $1.4 billion; BlackBerry sold its Cylance assets to Arctic Wolf in 2024. It no longer exists as an independent brand. B2B cybersecurity brand.

EAP is described by Crunchbase as an environmental consulting firm based in St. Petersburg, Florida, with industries in consulting and environmental services. It provides environmental consulting services to clients, but the input does not make clear its size, clients or ownership. A funding figure of $300 million is shown in April 2024, which seems large for a small consultancy and may reflect a financing or acquisition-related event. The name is generic and could be confused with other companies. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

EastLink is a tolled motorway in Melbourne, Australia, running about 39 kilometres from Donvale to Frankston and connecting the eastern and south-eastern suburbs, with its operator based in Ringwood. Customers are drivers paying tolls collected electronically. It opened in 2008 under a public-private partnership and is run by a private infrastructure operator. Crunchbase shows a $300 million financing in June 2024. Well-known road brand in Melbourne, with little reach beyond the city.

Emoney.cn (Yimeng) is a Shanghai-based Chinese provider of investment and financial information and software, best known for its stock-market analysis app that gives retail investors data, tools and advisory products. Customers are individual investors, and it earns subscription and service revenue. Crunchbase shows about CN¥1.8 billion in funding in 2015. A domestic fintech information brand in China, with a loyal user base but limited recognition abroad.

FloQast is a Los Angeles-area accounting software company, based in Sherman Oaks, that sells cloud software for month-end close, reconciliation and compliance, used by accounting teams at mid-market and large enterprises, and runs an accounting community. Customers pay subscriptions. Founded in 2013, it had raised over $300 million from investors including Insight Partners and Norwest, and has more than 3,000 customers. B2B software brand with limited consumer awareness.

Fungible was a Santa Clara, California start-up that designed a data processing unit (DPU) chip and software for data centres, to offload networking and storage tasks from servers. Customers were cloud and enterprise data centre operators. Founded in 2015, it raised about $300 million from investors including SoftBank and Norwest, and was acquired by Microsoft in 2023, so it no longer operates independently. B2B semiconductor brand with no consumer awareness.

HUMAN Security is a New York cybersecurity company that protects websites, apps, advertising and online platforms from bots, fraud and account takeover by verifying that online traffic comes from real humans. It was formerly White Ops and has grown through acquisitions. Customers are major publishers, ad-tech firms, retailers and banks, paying subscription and usage fees. Founded in 2012, it has raised about $300 million from investors including WestCap and Paladin. B2B brand with little consumer awareness.

Karvy Group is a Hyderabad-based Indian financial services group, known for stock broking, registrar and transfer services for mutual funds, wealth management, insurance distribution and data management. Its stock broking arm was embroiled in a 2019 scandal over misuse of client shares, leading to regulatory action from SEBI and the NSE and a collapse of its broking business. Crunchbase shows about $324 million of funding. Once a widely used brand among Indian retail investors, now damaged.

Kior is listed in the input as a Pasadena, Texas company in the beauty industry, described as an at-home medical-grade laser hair removal machine. However, a company named KiOR was a well-known Texas cellulosic biofuel start-up that filed for bankruptcy in 2014, so the input may be mixing two entities. The Crunchbase funding total of about $299 million and an October 2013 date match the biofuel company's history more than a beauty brand. Identity should be verified. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Kordsa is a Turkish industrial manufacturer, based in Izmit, Kocaeli, producing tyre reinforcement materials, such as nylon and polyester cord fabrics and tyre cord, as well as composite technologies and construction reinforcement. Customers are tyre makers such as Michelin, Goodyear and Bridgestone, and it has plants in Turkey, Brazil, Indonesia, Thailand and the US. Part of Sabanci Holding and listed on Borsa Istanbul (KORDS). B2B industrial brand with little consumer awareness.

Lakala is a Beijing-based Chinese payments and fintech company that provides card readers, mobile payment terminals and payment services for small merchants and consumers, along with credit card repayment and financial services. It earns transaction fees and service revenue. Founded in 2005, it has raised about $312 million from investors including Legend Capital. Well known to small merchants in China, with a consumer-facing payment app, but little recognition abroad.

Mucfc.com is the online platform of Merchants Union Consumer Finance (Zhaoshang Xiaofei Jinrong), a Shenzhen-area Chinese consumer finance company founded by China Merchants Bank and partners. It provides consumer loans and instalment credit through its apps, for tens of millions of customers. Crunchbase shows about CN¥2 billion of funding in 2018. Part of a major Chinese banking group, with strong domestic consumer finance recognition but little overseas awareness.

Photobox is a London-based online photo products company offering photo books, prints, cards, calendars and gifts in Europe, with brands that have included Photobox and Hofmann, and the group once owned Moonpig. Consumers upload photos online and order personalised products. Founded in 2000, it was backed by Electra Partners and Highland Capital and went through a restructuring in 2019-20. Crunchbase shows $305 million funding in 2014. A well-known consumer brand in the UK and Europe, with a gifting focus.

Privalia is a flash-sale online fashion retailer founded in Barcelona in 2006, offering discounted brand-name clothing, shoes and home goods to members in Spain, Italy, Mexico and Brazil. The input gives Sao Paulo in Brazil as its base. It raised about $295 million and was acquired by French group Vente-Privee (now Veepee) in 2016 for around EUR 500 million, so it operates as part of Veepee. Consumer brand with membership-based loyalty across southern Europe and Latin America.

PTT Global Chemical (GC) is Thailand's largest integrated petrochemical company, based in Bangkok and majority-owned by state energy group PTT. It makes olefins, polyethylene, polypropylene, styrene, ethylene oxide derivatives and aromatics, and has bioplastics and recycling initiatives, with plants in Thailand, plus operations in the US, China and Europe. Customers are packaging, automotive and industrial manufacturers. Listed on the Stock Exchange of Thailand (PTTGC), with revenue of several hundred billion baht. B2B industrial brand, though PTT is a known sponsor in Thailand.

Quality Systems, later renamed NextGen Healthcare, was an Irvine, California healthcare information technology company providing electronic health records, practice management and revenue cycle software to physician practices and community health centres.
